text: clinical epidemiologic research, analysts often need handle censoring, competing risks, intercurrent events (e.g. treatment switching), existing R packages typically separate tasks across different interfaces. cifmodeling provides unified, publication-ready toolkit integrates nonparametric estimation, regression modeling, visualization survival competing risks data. tools assist users following ways: Unified interface Kaplan–Meier Aalen–Johansen curves, survival competing risks handled Event() + formula + data syntax. Effects CIF scale: Fine-Gray models subdistribution hazards, polyreg() directly targets ratios CIFs (risk ratios, odds ratios, subdistribution hazard ratios), parameters align closely differences seen CIF curves. Coherent, joint modeling competing events: polyreg() models cause-specific CIFs together, parameterizing nuisance structure polytomous log odds products enforcing CIFs sum one. Curve-comparison tests: ciftest() provides log-rank, Gray, robust score, augmented score, rank-adaptive multiple-direction tests formula syntax. Tidy summaries reporting: support generics::tidy(), glance(), augment(), integrate polyreg() smoothly modelsummary broom-style tools. Publication-ready graphics built ggsurvfit ggplot2, including number--risk/CIF+CI tables, censoring/competing-risk/intercurrent-event marks, multi-panel layouts.

title: cifmodeling
text: Several excellent R packages exist survival competing risks analysis. survival package provides canonical API survival data. combination ggsurvfit package, survival::survfit() can produce publication-ready survival plots. CIF plots, however, integration general ecosystem less streamlined. cifmodeling fills gap offering cifplot() survival/CIF plots multi-panel figures via single, unified interface. Beyond providing unified interface, cifcurve() also extends survfit() targeted ways. unweighted survival data, reproduces standard Kaplan-Meier estimator Greenwood Tsiatis SEs unified set CI transformations. unweighted competing risks data, computes Aalen-Johansen CIFs Aalen-type delta-method SEs. default inference weighted curves uses influence-function based SEs (Deng Wang 2025). formulas vignette also describes weighted Kaplan–Meier estimator adjusted Greenwood variance. Xie Liu (2005) need fine-grained plot customization, can compute estimator keep survfit-compatible object cifcurve() (supply survfit object) style using ggsurvfit/ggplot2 layers. words: use cifcurve() estimation, use cifplot() / cifpanel() quick, high-quality figures, fall back ggplot ecosystem want full artistic control. causalRisk package offers IPW-based estimation counterfactual cumulative risks hazards. relevant treatment, censoring, missingness mechanisms must modeled explicitly. contrast, cifmodeling focuses nonparametric estimation direct CIF regression rather structural causal models. mets package specialized toolkit provides advanced methods competing risks analysis. cifmodeling::polyreg() focuses coherent modeling CIFs simultaneously estimate exposure effects terms RR//SHR. coherence can come longer runtimes large problems. prefer fitting separate regression models competing event specifically need Fine-Gray models (Fine Gray 1999) direct binomial models (Scheike, Zhang Gerds 2008), mets::cifreg() mets::binreg() excellent choices. short, cifmodeling provides unified high-level grammar estimation, visualization, direct CIF regression — something existing package currently offers one place.
